minutes.headline: Commission approved an earlier Hickory Hills lake drawdown for dam repairs and continued the 238 Fire Road 16 hearing for a site walk.
minutes.summary: The commission heard Hickory Hills' request to start the dam drawdown early for concrete and sluice repairs. It approved the request with the wording "as soon as possible". It also took an update on the 2020 lake treatment and continued several hearings, among them 99 Roost Street, two dock hearings and 238 Fire Road 16. It approved the Blood pool and garage notice of intent with conditions and backed the town exercising first refusal on 250 Howard Street. It also approved minutes and discussed enforcement items and chair procedure.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved Hickory Hills' request to start its dam drawdown early for concrete and sluice repairs, 6-0 by roll call.
The commission voted to support the town buying 250 Howard Street and forwarded the vote to the selectmen; funding was left to them.
The 238 Fire Road 16 hearing was continued to September 16, with a site walk planned for the Saturday before.
The commission approved the Blood pool and garage notice of intent with conditions on backwash plumbing, pool drainage and cleanup.
The 99 Roost Street hearing and two dock hearings were continued; the chair was authorized to pursue Stagecoach Road clearing and parking with town counsel.

why_it_matters: The Howard Street vote starts a possible town purchase that would draw on the conservation trust fund, grants or the town budget, mostly taxes, so residents may be asked to vote on funding.
The early drawdown and dam repairs change lake water levels at Hickory Hills for abutters and lake users, and several pending hearings could set rules for shoreline docks and floodplain building.
watch_next: September 16 meeting: continued hearings for 99 Roost Street, the dock/stairs matter and 238 Fire Road 16, plus ratification of the emergency tree-removal permits.
The Brewster/O'Brien deed restriction language, passed to town counsel, and the selectmen's handling of the 250 Howard Street purchase.
